classes.label: Bayesian Updater
classes.comment:
A structured probabilistic component that takes a prior probability
distribution and evidence, and produces a posterior distribution via
Bayes' theorem. In coordinate-framework terms (reasoning metamodel
§11.6): sequential Bayesian updating is a trajectory through
probability space — the prior de...

classes.label: Claim
classes.comment:
An assertion produced by a ReasoningActivity. Dual subclassing: IAO
information content entity (ontological grounding — a claim is about
something and is the output of a cognitive or computational process)
and PROV-O Entity (provenance interoperability — a claim is a thing
with provenance that ca...

classes.label: Combination Algebra
classes.comment:
The algebraic structure governing how constraint values combine. A
CombinationAlgebra specifies the combination operator (how values aggregate)
and the selection operator (how the best option is chosen).

BFO grounding: information content entity (IAO_0000030) — a specification
of combination sem...

classes.label: Confidence Assessment
classes.comment:
An assessment of evidential confidence attached to a Claim, with a
declared interpretive frame (S147-D1). The interpretive frame specifies
how the confidence value should be understood and combined:

  - Probability frame: confidence is a probability (0–1), combined via
    Bayesian updating, rep...

classes.label: Constraint
classes.comment:
Abstract constraint type. In the reasoning metamodel, constraints shape
the coordinate space through which reasoning navigates. The three-way
distinction (S146-D8, grounded by S147-D3): HardConstraint (boundary),
SoftConstraint (cost surface), GradedRule (truth-value surface).

Constraints are in...

classes.label: Control Action
classes.comment:
An action taken by a controller to enforce a safety constraint. A
ControlAction is a process — something that happens in time — as opposed
to the ControlStructure (an information entity specifying who can act) or
the SafetyConstraint (an information entity specifying what must hold).

BFO groundi...

classes.label: Control Loop
classes.comment:
A specific controller → actuator → controlled process → sensor → controller
feedback cycle within a broader ControlStructure. A ControlStructure may
contain multiple ControlLoops operating at different levels of the hierarchy.

Coordinate-framework grounding: a ControlLoop is the operational unit...

classes.label: Control Structure
classes.comment:
A hierarchical arrangement of controllers, controlled processes, and
feedback loops. The control structure describes the mechanisms that maintain
entity trajectories within safe NormativeRegions.

BFO grounding: information content entity (IAO_0000030) — a ControlStructure
is information about co...

classes.label: Coordination Heuristic
classes.comment:
A heuristic for care coordination and team management. Minimises
handoff count, maximises accountability continuity, and prefers known
competent teams.

Coordinate-framework grounding: minimise discontinuity in agent-assignment
dimensions — smooth agent transitions preserve contextual knowledge.

classes.label: Decision
classes.comment:
A choice among alternatives, produced by a ReasoningActivity. A Decision
records which alternative was selected, the reasoning context in which
the choice was made, and the justification. In coordinate-framework
terms, a Decision selects a trajectory through the coordinate space
from among the fe...

classes.label: Decision Mode
classes.comment:
Classification of the reasoning context's problem domain (S146-D5).
Determines which ReasoningComponents are activated. Phase 2 will
elaborate with Cynefin domain mapping (clear, complicated, complex,
chaotic) as ClassificationRegion instances (S147-D2).

BFO grounding: information content entity...

classes.label: Diagnostic Heuristic
classes.comment:
A heuristic for diagnostic reasoning. Generates hypotheses broadly
then prunes using discriminating evidence.

Coordinate-framework grounding: maximise information gain per reasoning
step — choose tests and observations that most efficiently reduce
uncertainty about the entity's position in the c...

classes.label: Evidence Item
classes.comment:
A specific piece of evidence within an EvidenceLine. An EvidenceItem
may be an observation, a measurement, a document reference, a dataset,
a prior Claim, or any other identifiable artifact that contributes to
the evidential basis of a Claim.

EvidenceItems carry their own provenance via PROV-O (...

classes.label: Evidence Line
classes.comment:
A coherent line of evidence supporting a Claim. An EvidenceLine groups
related EvidenceItems into an argument — a reason to believe the Claim.
A Claim may be supported by multiple EvidenceLines (converging evidence
from different sources), and each EvidenceLine may contain multiple
EvidenceItems ...

classes.label: FRAM Function
classes.comment:
A function description in the FRAM sense: a unit of activity with
six coupling aspects (Input, Output, Control, Precondition, Resource, Time).
A FRAMFunction describes what a function does, not the function itself.

BFO grounding: information content entity (IAO_0000030) — a FRAMFunction
is a des...

classes.label: Goal
classes.comment:
An intentional target — a directive specifying what the system is trying
to reach or maintain. In coordinate-framework terms (S147-D2, S146-D4),
a Goal references a GoalRegion in coordinate space: a region the system
is trying to reach or remain within. GoalRegions may be vague, multi-
dimensiona...

classes.label: Goal Ordering Heuristic
classes.comment:
A heuristic for sequencing goals and tasks. Prioritises prerequisite,
high-risk, irreversible, or high-information-gain tasks first.

Coordinate-framework grounding: prioritise movement along axes with
the highest goal-region proximity gradient — move fastest toward the
region boundaries that mat...

classes.label: Governance Heuristic
classes.comment:
A heuristic for governance-aware escalation. Requires human review
when confidence is low, novelty is high, explanation is weak, or
downstream risk is material.

Coordinate-framework grounding: escalate when the entity's position is
near the FormalisationFrontier or a NormativeRegion boundary — t...

classes.label: Graded Rule
classes.comment:
A constraint assigning a truth value in [0,1] to every point in the
coordinate space, representing the degree to which a business rule
or heuristic applies. PSL (Probabilistic Soft Logic) provides the
computational semantics: graded rules combine via convex optimisation
to find the most probable ...

classes.label: Hard Constraint
classes.comment:
A constraint defining a boundary that cannot be violated. In coordinate-
framework terms (S147-D3), a HardConstraint defines a NormativeRegion
or StaticBoundary in the coordinate space. The constraint is satisfied
when the entity's position is within the region; it is violated when
the position c...

classes.label: Heuristic
classes.comment:
A declarative heuristic — a practical rule of thumb that guides
reasoning without being formally mandatory. Heuristics are OWL
individuals with typed properties (S146-D6) declaring applicability
conditions, ordering logic, and authority basis.

In coordinate-framework terms (§7.4 of the coordinat...

classes.label: Heuristic Pack
classes.comment:
A named, versionable collection of heuristics applicable to a domain,
service line, or regulatory context. A HeuristicPack bundles the heuristics
that apply to a particular operational situation — selecting the right pack
is the first step in heuristic reasoning.

BFO grounding: information conte...

classes.label: Interpretive Frame
classes.comment:
The interpretive frame for a ConfidenceAssessment — determines how
the confidence value is understood and combined with other assessments.
Three frames are defined (S147-D1, stable since Session 46):

  - ProbabilityFrame: Bayesian probability semantics
  - FuzzyMembershipFrame: fuzzy set members...

classes.label: Knowledge Source
classes.comment:
An abstract type for knowledge inputs to reasoning. KnowledgeSources
are consulted by ReasoningActivities (via prov:used) and contribute
to the production of Claims and Decisions. Concrete subtypes include
clinical guidelines, regulatory instruments, population data sets,
expert knowledge, and he...

classes.label: Measure
classes.comment:
A projection onto a specific coordinate axis for evaluation. A Measure
defines how progress toward a Goal or compliance with a Constraint is
assessed — it selects one or more axes from the coordinate space and
specifies the assessment semantics (threshold, range, trend, rate).

In coordinate-fram...

classes.label: Obstacle
classes.comment:
A condition that constrains or impedes trajectories toward a Goal.
An Obstacle is descriptive information — it records a fact about
the environment that makes goal attainment harder. In coordinate-
framework terms, an Obstacle identifies a region or condition in the
coordinate space that the syst...

classes.label: Plan
classes.comment:
A sequence of intended actions toward a Goal. In coordinate-framework
terms, a Plan specifies a trajectory through the coordinate space
from the current position toward a GoalRegion, accounting for
Constraints and Obstacles.

BFO grounding: plan specification (IAO_0000104) — IAO defines plan
spec...

classes.label: Predictive Analytics
classes.comment:
A structured probabilistic component for population-level analysis
that does not target individual patient outcomes. Produces aggregate
probabilistic assessments: demand forecasting, resource utilisation
projections, population health trend analysis.

Distinguished from RiskCalculator and Prognos...

classes.label: Prognostic Model
classes.comment:
A structured probabilistic component that models time-to-event or
trajectory outcomes. Produces probability distributions over future
states at specified time horizons. In coordinate-framework terms:
a PrognosticModel projects trajectories forward through the
coordinate space, producing Probabili...

classes.label: Reasoning Activity
classes.comment:
A single reasoning episode — a bounded process in which knowledge sources
are consulted, constraints evaluated, and a decision or claim produced. Dual
subclassing: BFO process (ontological grounding) and PROV-O Activity
(provenance interoperability). Every ReasoningActivity has a context, may
use...

classes.label: Reasoning Agent
classes.comment:
An entity that bears responsibility for a reasoning activity — a human
practitioner, a software component, or a composite of both. Dual
subclassing: BFO material entity (ontological grounding) and PROV-O
Agent (provenance interoperability).

BFO grounding: material entity (BFO_0000040).
PROV-O al...

classes.label: Reasoning Component
classes.comment:
Abstract type for typed reasoning capabilities that can be activated
within a ReasoningContext. Concrete subtypes include deterministic
rule engines (Tier 1), inspectable logic components (Tier 2),
structured probabilistic models (new category per S147-D5), and
opaque probabilistic models (Tier 3...

classes.label: Reasoning Context
classes.comment:
The context within which a reasoning activity occurs. Captures the
domain position, decision mode, available knowledge sources, active
constraints, and applicable goals. A ReasoningContext is generically
dependent — it is information about the conditions of reasoning, not
the reasoning itself.

T...

classes.label: Resource Heuristic
classes.comment:
A heuristic for resource-allocation decisions. Prefers scarce-resource
preservation, continuity-preserving allocations, and local-capacity balancing.

Coordinate-framework grounding: minimise rate of change in resource-axis
dimensions — smooth allocation trajectories preserve capacity.

classes.label: Risk Calculator
classes.comment:
A BayesianUpdater with explicit validation metadata — a validated
population-level risk model. Distinguished from a generic
BayesianUpdater by the requirement for published validation data:
validation population characteristics, performance metrics
(AUC, sensitivity, specificity, calibration), an...

classes.label: Risk Heuristic
classes.comment:
A heuristic for risk recognition and escalation. Activates on
red-flag combinations, uncertainty plus severity, and vulnerable-population
markers.

Coordinate-framework grounding: increase monitoring density near
NormativeRegion boundaries — proximity to a constraint boundary
warrants heightened ...

classes.label: Safety Constraint
classes.comment:
A HardConstraint whose violation constitutes a safety hazard. Safety
constraints are the hardest of hard constraints — they define the
boundaries of safety-critical NormativeRegions that must never be crossed.

Coordinate-framework grounding: a SafetyConstraint defines a safety-critical
Normative...

classes.label: Soft Constraint
classes.comment:
A constraint defining a continuous cost or preference landscape over
the coordinate space. Every point in the space has a cost associated
with it; the system seeks to minimise cost or maximise preference.
A SoftConstraint shapes trajectories rather than bounding them.

In coordinate-framework ter...

classes.label: Structured Probabilistic Component
classes.comment:
Abstract type for validated probabilistic models — the new category
between Tier 2 (inspectable logic) and Tier 3 (opaque ML) per the
A6 reformulation (S147-D5).

Structured probabilistic components share three defining properties:
  1. Deterministic in mechanism — same inputs produce same output...

classes.label: Unsafe Control Action
classes.comment:
A ControlAction that leads to a hazard. The STPA method identifies
four types of unsafe control actions (the four ways boundary maintenance
can fail):

1. NotProvided: required action not taken — the controller fails to issue
   an action when the boundary is being approached. The trajectory cros...

classes.label: Unsafe Control Action Type
classes.comment:
A classification of the type of unsafe control action. The four STPA
types are the standard vocabulary for describing how a control action can
cause a hazard. This class is instantiated as a closed enumeration of four
named individuals.

BFO grounding: information content entity (IAO_0000030) — a...

classes.label: Variability Profile
classes.comment:
A description of how a FRAMFunction's performance varies. The
VariabilityProfile captures both internal variability (from within the
function itself) and external variability (from upstream coupling with
other functions).

Coordinate-framework grounding: describes the spread of actual trajectorie...

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:activatesComponent
objectProperties.label: activates component
objectProperties.comment:
Links a DecisionMode to the ReasoningComponent types it activates.
This is the routing mechanism: given a context's decision mode, the
system knows which components to engage. The routing is not exclusive
— modes may activate overlapping sets of components, with higher
modes activating all compon...

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:applicableToContext
objectProperties.label: applicable to context
objectProperties.comment:
Links a Heuristic to the ReasoningContext types that activate it.
A heuristic is applicable to a context when the context's properties
(goal type, decision mode, domain) match the heuristic's activation
criteria.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:applicableToDomain
objectProperties.label: applicable to domain
objectProperties.comment:
Links a Heuristic or HeuristicPack to the DomainIdentity it applies to.
Both individual heuristics and entire packs can declare domain applicability.
Domain-specific heuristics override or supplement the default set for that
operational context.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:composedWith
objectProperties.label: composed with
objectProperties.comment:
Expresses that two Constraints interact and should be evaluated
together. Symmetric — if A is composedWith B, then B is composedWith A.
Composition may be necessary when constraints share variables, conflict,
or must be satisfied jointly for a decision to be valid.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:coupledWith
objectProperties.label: coupled with
objectProperties.comment:
Symmetric coupling between FRAMFunctions. If function A is coupled
with function B, then B is coupled with A. Coupling is the mechanism by
which variability propagates — a variable output from one function becomes
a variable input to another.

Coordinate-framework grounding: coupling propagates t...

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:enforces
objectProperties.label: enforces
objectProperties.comment:
Links a ControlAction to the SafetyConstraint it enforces. A
ControlAction is always issued to enforce some constraint — this property
makes that connection explicit and auditable.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasAuthorityBasis
objectProperties.label: has authority basis
objectProperties.comment:
Links a Heuristic to the KnowledgeSource that justifies its use.
A heuristic is not an arbitrary rule — it is grounded in evidence,
clinical guidelines, domain expertise, or regulatory requirements.
This property makes that grounding explicit and auditable.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasCombinationAlgebra
objectProperties.label: has combination algebra
objectProperties.comment:
Links a Constraint to its CombinationAlgebra. Functional — each
constraint has exactly one combination algebra. This determines how
the constraint's values aggregate and how the best-satisfying option
is selected when multiple options are available.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasConfidence
objectProperties.label: has confidence
objectProperties.comment:
Links a Claim to its ConfidenceAssessment. A Claim may have multiple
confidence assessments (e.g. from different evaluation methods or at
different points in time), each with its own interpretive frame.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasConstraint
objectProperties.label: has constraint
objectProperties.comment:
Links a ReasoningContext to the Constraint(s) that shape the
reasoning. Constraints include hard boundaries (HardConstraint),
cost surfaces (SoftConstraint), and truth-value surfaces
(GradedRule).

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasContext
objectProperties.label: has context
objectProperties.comment:
Links a ReasoningActivity to the ReasoningContext in which it
was conducted. Every reasoning episode occurs within a specific
context that determines available knowledge, active constraints,
applicable goals, and the decision mode.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasControlLoop
objectProperties.label: has control loop
objectProperties.comment:
Links a ControlStructure to its constituent ControlLoops. A
ControlStructure may contain multiple loops operating at different
levels of the hierarchy.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasControlledProcess
objectProperties.label: has controlled process
objectProperties.comment:
Links a ControlLoop to the controlled process — the activity or
system whose trajectory the loop monitors and corrects. The controlled
process is what can cross a NormativeRegion boundary if not properly
managed.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasController
objectProperties.label: has controller
objectProperties.comment:
Links a ControlLoop to its controller — the entity (agent, system,
or role) that issues ControlActions. The controller can be a person,
an automated system, a regulatory body, or any other thing that has
authority to take corrective action.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasDecisionMode
objectProperties.label: has decision mode
objectProperties.comment:
Links a ReasoningContext to its decision mode classification (S146-D5).
Functional — a context has exactly one active decision mode. The
decision mode determines which ReasoningComponents are activated.

Phase 2 (Step 2.2) will elaborate DecisionMode with Cynefin domain
mapping and routing rules.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasEvidence
objectProperties.label: has evidence
objectProperties.comment:
Links an EvidenceLine to the EvidenceItem(s) that compose it.
Each EvidenceItem is a specific artifact (observation, measurement,
document, prior claim) contributing to the line of evidence.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasFunctionControl
objectProperties.label: has function control
objectProperties.comment:
Links a FRAMFunction to its control — conditions or constraints that
regulate how the function is executed. Controls correspond to SafetyConstraints
and governance obligations that bound the function's trajectory.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasFunctionInput
objectProperties.label: has function input
objectProperties.comment:
Links a FRAMFunction to its input — what initiates or is transformed
by the function. In coordinate-framework terms: the region of coordinate
space that the function starts from.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasFunctionOutput
objectProperties.label: has function output
objectProperties.comment:
Links a FRAMFunction to its output — what the function produces or
transforms its input into. In coordinate-framework terms: the region of
coordinate space that the function moves toward.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasFunctionPrecondition
objectProperties.label: has function precondition
objectProperties.comment:
Links a FRAMFunction to its precondition — what must be true before
the function can execute. Preconditions define the entry conditions for
the function's coordinate-space transformation.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasFunctionResource
objectProperties.label: has function resource
objectProperties.comment:
Links a FRAMFunction to its resource — what is consumed or used
(but not transformed) during function execution. Resources constrain
when and how often the function can execute.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasFunctionTime
objectProperties.label: has function time
objectProperties.comment:
Links a FRAMFunction to its time aspect — temporal constraints on
when and for how long the function executes. In coordinate-framework
terms: the time axis is always present as a dimension; this property
makes the temporal bounds of a function explicit.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasGoal
objectProperties.label: has goal
objectProperties.comment:
Links a ReasoningContext to the Goal(s) that the reasoning is
directed toward. A context may have multiple goals (which may
be complementary, competing, or hierarchically decomposed).

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasInterpretiveFrame
objectProperties.label: has interpretive frame
objectProperties.comment:
Links a ConfidenceAssessment to its InterpretiveFrame. Functional —
each confidence assessment has exactly one interpretive frame that
determines how the confidence value is understood and combined.
A ConfidenceAssessment without a declared frame is meaningless.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasKnowledgeSource
objectProperties.label: has knowledge source
objectProperties.comment:
Links a ReasoningContext to the KnowledgeSource(s) available for
consultation during reasoning. This includes guidelines, regulatory
instruments, heuristics, and any other information inputs.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasMeasure
objectProperties.label: has measure
objectProperties.comment:
Links a Goal to the Measure(s) used to assess progress toward it.
Each Measure is a named projection onto a coordinate axis,
defining how attainment of the goal is evaluated.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasMember
objectProperties.label: has member
objectProperties.comment:
Links a HeuristicPack to its constituent heuristics. A pack contains
one or more heuristics that collectively cover the reasoning situation
for which the pack is designed.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasObstacle
objectProperties.label: has obstacle
objectProperties.comment:
Links a ReasoningContext to Obstacle(s) identified as impeding
progress toward the context's goals.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasPlan
objectProperties.label: has plan
objectProperties.comment:
Links a Decision to the Plan that implements it. A Decision may
have zero plans (immediate action) or one plan (a structured
sequence of intended actions toward a goal).

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasPosterior
objectProperties.label: has posterior
objectProperties.comment:
Links a BayesianUpdater to its posterior probability distribution,
represented as a Claim. The posterior is the output of Bayesian
updating — the refined distribution after incorporating evidence.
As a Claim, it carries confidence assessment, evidence lines, and
PROV-O provenance (prov:wasGenerat...

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasPrior
objectProperties.label: has prior
objectProperties.comment:
Links a BayesianUpdater to its prior probability distribution,
represented as a Claim (an assertion about the prior state of
knowledge). The prior Claim carries its own ConfidenceAssessment
with ProbabilityFrame, and its own evidence chain.

The choice to type the prior as a Claim (rather than a ...

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasSafetyEvidence
objectProperties.label: has safety evidence
objectProperties.comment:
Links a SafetyConstraint to a Claim that provides evidence of its
satisfaction or violation. This reuses the SEPIO evidence architecture
(Sections 5 and 6) for safety compliance: a safety constraint is satisfied
when there is a Claim (backed by EvidenceLines and EvidenceItems) that
the controlled...

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasUnsafeActionType
objectProperties.label: has unsafe action type
objectProperties.comment:
Links an UnsafeControlAction to its STPA type classification.
Provides a structured vocabulary for describing how the control action
caused or contributed to a hazard.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hasVariabilityProfile
objectProperties.label: has variability profile
objectProperties.comment:
Links a FRAMFunction to its VariabilityProfile. Functional — each
function has exactly one variability profile (though the profile may
describe multiple variability sources). The variability profile is the
primary input for FRAM resonance analysis.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:hierarchicallyControls
objectProperties.label: hierarchically controls
objectProperties.comment:
A transitive hierarchical control relationship. Enables modelling
of multi-level governance hierarchies, e.g.: HSE → COSHH regulator →
operator → machine. Transitivity means that if A hierarchically controls
B and B hierarchically controls C, then A hierarchically controls C.

Coordinate-framewor...

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:monitoredBy
objectProperties.label: monitored by
objectProperties.comment:
Links a SafetyConstraint to the ControlLoop that monitors and
enforces it. This is the operational connection between the constraint
(the rule that must hold) and the mechanism (the loop that detects
violations and issues ControlActions to correct them).

A SafetyConstraint may be monitored by mu...

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:overrides
objectProperties.label: overrides
objectProperties.comment:
Links a Heuristic to the Heuristic it overrides. Used when a domain-
or context-specific heuristic replaces a more general default.

Override events are recorded via PROV-O: prov:wasGeneratedBy on the
overriding heuristic links to the ReasoningActivity that decided the
override, preserving full p...

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:producedDecision
objectProperties.label: produced decision
objectProperties.comment:
Links a ReasoningActivity to the Decision it produced. Complements
prov:wasGeneratedBy (which links from the Decision back to the
Activity). A ReasoningActivity may produce zero or more Decisions
(zero if the activity produces Claims but no decision).

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:supportedBy
objectProperties.label: supported by
objectProperties.comment:
Links a Claim to the EvidenceLine(s) that support it. A Claim
may have multiple evidence lines representing converging evidence
from independent sources. The absence of any evidence lines
indicates an unsupported assertion.

objectProperties.name: ontara-rsn:transitionsTo
objectProperties.label: transitions to
objectProperties.comment:
Links one DecisionMode to another that the context may transition to.
A mode transition is a ReasoningActivity — the recognition that the
problem character has changed. Transitions may be triggered by new
evidence, escalation conditions, or stabilisation events.

datatypeProperties.label: has confidence interval
datatypeProperties.comment:
Records the confidence interval or bounds on the component's
probabilistic output. Free-text for now — structured interval
representation (lower bound, upper bound, confidence level) is
a candidate for future elaboration.

Examples: '95% CI: 9.2%-15.8%', 'Prediction interval: 3-18 months'.

datatypeProperties.label: has confidence value
datatypeProperties.comment:
The numeric confidence value (typically 0–1) of a ConfidenceAssessment.
The meaning of this value depends on the InterpretiveFrame:
  - ProbabilityFrame: Bayesian probability
  - FuzzyMembershipFrame: degree of membership
  - PreferenceWeightFrame: preference strength

Functional — each assessmen...

datatypeProperties.label: has external variability
datatypeProperties.comment:
Describes the external variability of a FRAMFunction — variation
propagated from upstream coupled functions. A function with low internal
variability can still have high effective variability if its inputs are
highly variable.

datatypeProperties.label: has hazard description
datatypeProperties.comment:
A natural-language description of the hazard associated with a
SafetyConstraint or UnsafeControlAction. For SafetyConstraint: describes
what harm results from violating the constraint. For UnsafeControlAction:
describes the hazard the unsafe action caused or could cause.

datatypeProperties.label: has identity element
datatypeProperties.comment:
The identity element of the CombinationAlgebra. String type to
accommodate "not applicable" for algebras such as PSLConvexOptimisation
where no scalar identity exists. For semirings, this is the identity
of the combination operator (addition or multiplication).

datatypeProperties.label: has internal variability
datatypeProperties.comment:
Describes the internal variability of a FRAMFunction — variation
arising from within the function itself (e.g. skill variation, equipment
drift, cognitive load). Free-text for now; structured variability
scales are a candidate for future elaboration.

datatypeProperties.label: has ordering logic
datatypeProperties.comment:
Describes the ordering or selection logic of the Heuristic in natural
language. This is the human-readable rationale for why this heuristic
applies and how it ranks or selects among options. Required for
interpretability and governance audit.

datatypeProperties.label: has performance metric
datatypeProperties.comment:
Records a performance metric from the component's validation.
Free-text for now — structured metric representation (AUC, C-statistic,
calibration slope, sensitivity, specificity) is a candidate for
future elaboration. Multiple values may be asserted.

datatypeProperties.label: has priority
datatypeProperties.comment:

datatypeProperties.label: has truth value range
datatypeProperties.comment:
Documents the truth-value range of a GradedRule. Typically "[0,1]"
for standard fuzzy logic and PSL, but may differ for other graded
logics. String type to accommodate non-standard ranges.

datatypeProperties.label: has validation population
datatypeProperties.comment:

validated. Free-text description of cohort characteristics, size,
